principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status + NN/g #9 Help users recover from errors + WCAG 2.2 §3.3.1 Error Identification
location: POST /sign-in and POST /sign-up (server actions in src/app/sign-in/actions.ts + src/app/sign-up/actions.ts; underlying createSession() in src/lib/auth/session.ts)
problem: Sign-up and sign-in both COMPLETE on the server (user row created — confirmed via /api/auth/has-recovery-email?u=<new> returning 200), but no session cookie is set on the response. The server action returns x-action-redirect: /projects;push, the client navigates to /projects, the auth() lookup finds no session, and the user is silently dropped back onto the sign-in form. Observed end-to-end three times with fresh accounts (auditor7748711, etc.). No toast, no console error, no visible failure — the form just re-renders with cleared password and no message. The funnel is functionally broken: there is no way for a brand-new visitor to actually use the app.
fix: Server-side: confirm the cookies().set() inside createSession() in src/lib/auth/session.ts is being awaited correctly under the React server-action runtime — Next 16 + Vercel can lose cookie writes if the response is committed before the async cookie jar flush. Either (a) move the cookie write to a route handler the form posts to via fetch, or (b) verify the libsql/turso write completes inside the action's transaction and that NextAuth's `Set-Cookie` headers aren't being stripped by Vercel's edge middleware. As an immediate UX guard, add a client-side post-submit check: after the action resolves with ok:true, call `/api/auth/me` (add it if missing) and surface a toast `Sign-in failed — please try again` if the session lookup returns null. Right now success is indistinguishable from failure.

principle: NN/g #3 User control and freedom + NN/g #5 Error prevention + Jakob's Law (familiarity of forgot-password affordance)
location: src/app/sign-in/SignInForm.tsx lines 128–134 — the disabled fallback path of the 'Forgot password?' UI
problem: The 'Forgot password?' element below the Sign In button is conditionally a real link only when /api/auth/has-recovery-email returns true for the typed username. For every brand-new free-tier account (which has no recovery email by definition until they add one in Settings — a setting they can only reach when signed in), the element renders as a non-interactive <span class="cursor-help" title="Add a recovery email in Settings to enable password reset.">. The text, position, font and colour are nearly identical to the working-link variant. A user who genuinely forgets their password has no escape hatch — the only recovery copy lives in a hover-only title tooltip that the user cannot reach by keyboard or touch, and tells them to do something (Settings) that requires being signed in. This is a hard lock-out for the most common auth failure mode.
fix: Two options, both required: (1) Replace the disabled <span> with a real <Link> to /sign-in/forgot regardless of recovery-email status. /sign-in/forgot already gracefully handles the no-recovery-email case (existing behavior per the route comment). The probe response should drive the *destination*, not the *existence* of the link. (2) If you keep the conditional, render visible inline copy under the form — `No password reset is available — sign up for a new account or contact support` — not a tooltip. Tooltips are not accessible on touch and not WCAG-conformant for primary recovery paths.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (3:1 minimum for UI component boundaries)
location: src/app/globals.css `.frame-strong` (line 266–268) applied to all auth-form <input> elements in src/app/sign-in/SignInForm.tsx and src/app/sign-up/SignUpForm.tsx
problem: All three sign-up inputs (and the sign-in password field at rest) render with border `#363636` against background `#0a0a0a`. Measured contrast ratio: 1.68:1. WCAG 2.2 §1.4.11 requires 3:1 for UI component boundaries. The visual result is severe — the Password and Confirm Password fields read as floating labels with a single underline hairline; a first-time visitor cannot tell whether the input area exists or how big it is. This is the single biggest visual affordance failure on the most-judged surface in the app.
fix: Bump `--color-border-strong` from `#363636` to `#5a5a5a` (4.05:1 against `#0a0a0a` — comfortably passes), or apply a faint inset background to the inputs themselves: `input.frame-strong { background: #1a1a1a; }`. The inset-bg option costs no contrast budget and brings the inputs visually onto the same elevation as the .card body so they read as a recessed slot instead of a floating line. Either change touches one CSS token / one rule.

principle: Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy (the hero should not consume the entire above-fold) + Fitts's Law (the primary action should be the largest, closest target — here it is below the fold)
location: src/app/sign-up/page.tsx + src/app/sign-in/page.tsx + src/app/sign-in/forgot/page.tsx — `<Logo />` rendered without an explicit `width` inside a `max-w-md` (448px) wrapper
problem: On a typical 1440×900 desktop the 448×448 logo + 32px padding consumes 480px of the 720px useful viewport height before any form input appears. The 'Username' label sits at y≈540, the Submit button at y≈800. On a 1024×768 laptop the form button is fully below the fold. On mobile 375×667 (older iPhone SE — still common) the logo eats ~340px (1/2 the viewport), then the keyboard takes another 270px, leaving no usable form area at all. The hero is also the only visual content on the page — there is no headline, no value proposition, no microcopy — so it cannot earn the 1:1 aspect-ratio square it occupies. The recent commit `fb9f530 polish(auth): logo fills panel width on auth pages` overshot.
fix: Cap the logo: in src/components/ui/Logo.tsx default `width` to 192px (or expose `size="hero" | "compact"`) and have all three auth pages call `<Logo width={192} />`. Wrap the lockup in `flex items-center gap-3` with an `<h1>` next to it reading 'Create account' / 'Sign in' / 'Reset password' — that promotes a heading (fixing UX-V3-005) and gives the page a real first line of dialogue. Move the recovered ~250px of vertical space into form padding so the inputs breathe.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info and Relationships + §2.4.6 Headings and Labels
location: src/app/sign-in/page.tsx, src/app/sign-up/page.tsx, src/app/sign-in/forgot/page.tsx — all three render `<Card title="...">` whose title is a <span>, with NO <h1> elsewhere on the page
problem:
document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6').length === 0 on /sign-in and /sign-up. Card primitive renders its title inside a (src/components/ui/Card.tsx line 45). Screen-reader heading navigation (rotor / shortcuts) finds nothing on the public funnel — these users can't jump to the form by heading. SEO and assistive-tech outline both treat these pages as headingless documents. Library and other inner pages DO have `

LIBRARY

` etc., so this is a regression specific to the auth pages.
fix:
In src/components/ui/Card.tsx, render the title as an `

` instead of `` (it's already a section title — semantically correct). Then in each auth page, add an `

` (or visible — see UX-V3-004 for the visible lockup option) above the card with the page name — 'Sign in to Mini Manager', 'Create your Mini Manager account', 'Reset your password'. The visible alternative is preferred. Same h1 should replace the `Mini Manager` currently sitting under the Logo — that span is dead a11y weight.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — 24×24 CSS pixels MUST, 44×44 recommended for AA confidence on touch
location: All <input> elements in src/app/sign-in/SignInForm.tsx + src/app/sign-up/SignUpForm.tsx (37px tall measured); 'Sign in' top-nav link in 404/share layout (31px); 'Back to Mini Manager' CTA on /r/404 (31px)
problem: Measured heights: form inputs render at 37px tall (not 44px); the top-nav SIGN IN button and the public 404's CTA are both 31px tall. WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 passes at 24×24 minimum, but the global CSS comment at src/app/globals.css line 13 explicitly aims for 44px on mobile. The current values fall short — particularly the public 404's CTA, which is the only way back for an outside user who landed on a dead share link.
fix: Raise `.tap-target` min-height to 44px globally (currently looks like it resolves to ~37px). On the input styling: add `min-height: 44px` to the auth-form input class composition (it's already `py-2` ≈ 8+8 + a roughly 21px line — bump to `py-3` and tighten the font padding). On the public-layout nav button, use `<Button size="md">` (36px minimum) at the absolute lowest — and `size="lg"` (44px) preferred for the 404's primary CTA.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + Refactoring UI §3 Typography (one wordmark per page)
location: src/components/ui/Logo.tsx + src/app/sign-up/page.tsx — Logo image has alt='Mini Manager' AND the page renders `Mini Manager` immediately afterwards
problem: Screen-reader users hear 'Mini Manager. Mini Manager.' because the logo `<Image>` carries alt='Mini Manager' and the sibling sr-only span repeats it. The Logo primitive already exposes a `decorative` prop (src/components/ui/Logo.tsx line 12–14) for exactly this case, but the auth pages don't use it. The 'CREATE ACCOUNT' span inside the Card is announced third. So the announcement is 'Mini Manager, Mini Manager, Create account' — twice the brand, never the page name as a heading.
fix: Either (a) pass `decorative` to <Logo /> on the auth pages and let the sr-only span carry the brand name (currently it's redundant and not a heading), or (b) drop the sr-only span entirely and let the image alt carry the brand. Coupled with UX-V3-005 — add a visible or sr-only `<h1>` describing the *page* not the *brand*.

principle: NN/g #5 Error prevention + Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy (the primary action should be disabled until it can succeed)
location: src/app/sign-up/SignUpForm.tsx line 186 + src/app/sign-in/SignInForm.tsx line 113 — Submit button only disabled on `isPending` (and on 'taken' for sign-up)
problem: The Create Account / Sign In primary button is enabled the instant the page loads — with no fields filled, no validation, nothing. Clicking it fires a server round-trip that returns 'Wrong username or password' (or for sign-up triggers required-attribute browser native error). This trains users to click before reading. Tools like 1Password autosubmit will also fire pointlessly. Standard practice (Polaris, Material, Carbon, every auth UI in the wild) is to disable the primary action until at least the required fields contain text.
fix: Add a guard: `disabled={isPending || !username.trim() || password.length < PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH || (form === 'signup' && password !== confirm)}`. For sign-up, also wire the username uniqueness probe — it already runs (line 53–73); just include `check.kind !== 'ok'` in the disabled condition (sign-up already checks `taken` but not idle/checking). This is one expression change per form.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow + Apple HIG (form usability with on-screen keyboard)
location: src/app/sign-up/page.tsx + src/app/sign-in/page.tsx — `min-h-screen flex items-start md:items-center` wrapper
screenshot: screenshots_v3/01-signup-desktop-1440.png + (mobile reproduction by computed CSS — viewport reduce was unavailable, see 'needs_human' caveat)
problem: On mobile, the logo image takes ~280–340px square (capped by viewport minus 48px padding), leaving roughly 380–470px of remaining vertical viewport for the form before the soft keyboard appears. With the keyboard up (~280px on iOS, ~330px on Android), the auth form is squeezed below the keyboard or vanishes entirely on a 568px-tall iPhone SE. The `items-start` modifier on mobile is the right instinct, but doesn't help when the logo itself is huge.
fix: Same as UX-V3-004 — cap the logo width. Additionally, on mobile, swap layout to a horizontal lockup: logo (48–64px) + h1 wordmark side-by-side, leaving the entire below-the-header viewport for the form. This also avoids the awkward 'scroll past brand to find form' on a quick re-login.

principle: Refactoring UI §6 Shadows and Depth + §9 CRT Aesthetic (mix-blend-mode interactions)
location: src/components/ui/Logo.tsx — `mix-blend-mode: screen` on the brand image PLUS body::before scanline overlay at z-index 9998
problem: The logo uses `mix-blend-mode: screen` to drop out the PNG's black background. The body::before scanline overlay sits at z-index 9998 with `mix-blend-mode: overlay`. The interaction produces a faint repeating-line texture *inside* the logo's cyan engraving, slightly muddying the artwork — visible as a sub-pixel shimmer on the logo's flat cyan fields. Cosmetic, but it reads as if the print quality of the artwork is slightly degraded.
fix: On the Logo wrapper, isolate the blend context: add `isolation: isolate` to the logo's wrapping element, OR raise the logo to a z-index above 9998 with `position: relative` and let the scanlines render below the artwork. Cheaper alternative: replace the PNG with an inline SVG of the artwork, then the cyan strokes can be true cyan with text-shadow glow and no blend-mode trick is needed at all.

principle: Polaris — empty states must explain what goes here, why it's valuable, and what to do first
location: Sign-up funnel — there is no value proposition copy anywhere on /sign-up or /sign-in
problem: The sign-up page tells the user *what to do* (enter username and password) but never *why*. There is no microcopy under the brand or above the form explaining what Mini Manager actually is. A visitor who arrives from a shared recipe link, a Reddit mention, or a search result has to take it on faith. The page metadata description ('A wargaming + painting companion…') is in layout.tsx but never appears in the rendered page. Aesthetic-Usability Effect aside, you're asking for a password before describing the product.
fix: Add a single-line tagline below the lockup (or in place of the giant logo): `Plan armies. Track every model. Build paint recipes from a cross-brand library.` Use h2-sized text. This is the page's only chance to convert a curious visitor into an account.

principle: Apple HIG (form fields below the fold reduce completion) + WCAG 2.2 §2.4.6 Headings and Labels
location: src/app/sign-up/SignUpForm.tsx — no password-strength indicator, no character requirement hint before submit attempt
problem: The Password field on /sign-up has no inline hint about the minimum length (PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH from validation.ts). Users discover the requirement only by typing too few characters and hitting Submit, then reading the StatusPill error. This is a Hick's-Law + error-prevention miss. The Confirm Password field also has no real-time match indicator — you only learn passwords mismatch on Submit.
fix:
Below the Password input add a `
Minimum {PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH} characters
`. Below the Confirm input add a live mirror: `{confirm.length > 0 && (confirm === password ? matches : doesn't match yet)}`. Both are 3-line additions per field.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards (visual treatment for clickable vs decorative text)
location: src/app/sign-in/SignInForm.tsx line 128–134 — disabled 'Forgot password?' span styled almost identically to the link variant
problem: Beyond the lock-out flaw flagged in UX-V3-002, the visual treatment of the disabled 'Forgot password?' is at most a single shade darker (`--color-fg-subtle` #8a8a8a vs `--color-fg-muted` #a0a0a0). A user cannot tell visually whether the link works without hovering and reading the tooltip. The `cursor: help` is also a non-standard signal — most users don't recognise it as 'disabled'.
fix: Subsumed by the fix in UX-V3-002 (replace the conditional disabled span with a real link to /sign-in/forgot in all cases). If the conditional rendering MUST stay, render the disabled variant as static body copy without the question-mark CTA shape: 'Password reset requires a recovery email.' — no underline, no link affordance, no `cursor: help`. The pattern 'looks like a link, isn't a link' is the worst of both worlds.

principle: Refactoring UI §1 Hierarchy + Laws of UX (Von Restorff — the primary action should stand out)
location: src/components/ui/Card.tsx — card-header span 'CREATE ACCOUNT' / 'SIGN IN' / 'RESET PASSWORD'
problem: The card-header label is 13px mono in `--color-fg-muted` (#a0a0a0). This is the same visual weight as the field labels USERNAME / PASSWORD below it. There is no hierarchical distinction between the card title (which scopes the whole form) and the field labels (which scope a single input). A scan of the form reads as 4 sibling labels of equal importance: CREATE ACCOUNT / USERNAME / PASSWORD / CONFIRM PASSWORD.
fix: In src/app/globals.css `.card-header`, bump the colour to `--color-fg` (#f5f5f5) and add `font-weight: 500`. Keeps the uppercase-mono CRT vibe, but the card now has a distinct visual rank above its field labels. Alternative (cleaner once UX-V3-005 lands): drop the card-header text entirely on auth pages and let the page-level h1 carry the title.

principle: §9 Vintage Terminal / CRT — escape hatch for users who cannot read scanline overlays
location: src/app/globals.css body::before + body::after; .crt-off class declared but no UI to toggle it
problem: The CRT overlay (scanlines + vignette) is well-tuned — subtle, performance-safe, applied via pseudo-elements with pointer-events: none. The codebase even exposes `html.crt-off` to disable it (globals.css line 155–158). But there is no user-facing control to set that class. A user with astigmatism, motion sensitivity, or who simply finds the texture distracting has no way to opt out short of opening DevTools. §9 of the rubric explicitly calls out the need for an escape hatch.
fix: Add a 'Display' or 'Accessibility' section in /settings with a toggle: `CRT screen overlay [on/off]`. On change, write `html.crt-off` and persist in localStorage. Pre-rendering: on layout.tsx read a cookie/localStorage shim to avoid a flash on load. ~30 lines of code, no design budget needed.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.4.7 Focus Visible — fractional border-width can render as 0 on some browsers
location: All elements using `.frame-strong` and the auth-form inputs — computed border-width reads as `0.666667px`
problem: Measured border-width on the form inputs is 0.666667px — Tailwind's `border` (1px) appears to be scaled by an enclosing `transform: scale()` or rem rounding. Sub-pixel borders render inconsistently across browsers — on Chrome/Edge they often disappear entirely on standard-density displays. This compounds UX-V3-003: the border is BOTH too low-contrast AND occasionally not drawn at all.
fix: Search the codebase for any `transform: scale()` on a parent of the form (likely the source — possibly the body's `font-size` interpolation). Replace with explicit `border-width: 1px` on `.frame-strong` and ensure no parent transform downscales it. Verify computed border-width = 1.0px on each input via DevTools.

principle: Refactoring UI §3 Typography (use real content) + Polaris (every empty state must invite action)
problem: The 404 state of a shared recipe (a public surface that *outsiders* land on when a recipe is unpublished or the link is wrong) shows a heading, one line of body, and one CTA that just says 'Back to Mini Manager'. A non-user who arrived from a community link gets zero hook — no description of what Mini Manager *is*, no secondary CTA to create their own recipes, no 'Browse public recipes' link. This is one of the few organic acquisition pages and it terminates the funnel.
fix: Add a secondary CTA below the back-link: `[ Create your own paint recipes — sign up free ]`. Add a single tagline above it (same as UX-V3-011): `Mini Manager is a paint recipe + wishlist tool for miniature painters.` The page already has the brand chrome — completing the elevator pitch here costs ~50 LOC.

location: src/app/sign-up/SignUpForm.tsx — the gap between Username status pill and the next form field
problem: The username field reserves a `min-h-[20px]` slot for the live-check StatusPill (checking… / available / taken). When idle (no input) the slot still consumes 20px, creating a phantom gap that makes the Username field appear visually 'orphaned' from the Password field below it. The form's `space-y-4` does the right thing between fields, but the empty status slot turns that into `space-y-4 + 20px` selectively for one field.
fix:
Conditionally render the wrapper: `{check.kind !== 'idle' &&
…
}` — when idle, no slot, no orphan gap. Or animate the slot height with a 150ms ease to soften the appearance.
